name: Experiencing Marine Sanctuaries
summary: Experiencing Marine Sanctuaries is a South Australian not-for-profit that ran guided community snorkel tours in marine parks, with marine biologists on hand to identify the sea life. Tour sites included Noarlunga Reef, Aldinga Reef, Port Willunga and Second Valley, and the annual giant cuttlefish snorkel at Stony Point near Whyalla. The organisation has announced that it is shutting down operations.
standouts: Not-for-profit program based, with permission, on New Zealand's Experiencing Marine Reserves program
Coordinators are qualified first aid, snorkelling and/or diving instructors
Marine biologists on hand to identify marine life on community snorkels
Inclusive gear including a Mobi Chair floating beach wheelchair, reef boards and magnifying masks
checkNotes: NO TRIPS LISTED, PLEASE CHECK FIRST. The page https://www.emsau.org/ems-shutting-down/ says EMS has been significantly impacted by the harmful algal bloom and that operations will be shutting down. Its page data gives a publish date of 28 April 2026; the page shows no date itself. It is not linked from the menu or the home page, and the rest of the site still advertises tours (the home page was edited in July 2026 and still shows a Book Tour button and a CuttleFest July 2025 button). Because the site says operations are shutting down, no trip is listed here. Confirm with the operator whether anything still runs before publishing a page. WHAT THE SITE WOULD OTHERWISE SUPPORT. One trip type, guided community snorkel tours (the home page heading is Guided Community Snorkelling and VR Tours; the booking page is called EMS Community Tours). Names, dates, times and prices for the individual tours sit only inside an embedded Rezdy catalogue (https://emsau.rezdy.com/catalog/303487/tours on https://www.emsau.org/ems-community-tours/, and a carousel widget on the home page). That catalogue was not opened under the rules, and the site's own text gives no tour prices, so any trip would have prices [] and its booking link would be the tour page https://www.emsau.org/ems-community-tours/. The home page Book Tour button links to the storefront https://emsau.rezdy.com. rezdyAlias is emsau because that account belongs to EMS itself. Facts the site states for the community tours (FAQ and home page): small groups led by qualified snorkel guides, with marine biologists on hand to identify marine life; locations named are Noarlunga Reef, Aldinga Reef, Port Willunga and Second Valley (home page) and Seacliff Beach, Second Valley Beach, Port Noarlunga Reef and Stony Point near Whyalla during CuttleFest in July (inclusive page); ages 5 and over depending on the event, and children 15 and under must be accompanied in the water by a parent or guardian; swimmers must be able to swim any stroke at least 25 metres; a wetsuit is mandatory and provided with boots (gloves and hoods on colder snorkels such as CuttleFest); time in the water is typically 30 to 45 minutes; arrive 30 minutes before the start; sessions can be rescheduled or cancelled for weather or shark sightings. Prices are in AUD and include GST and a booking fee. Concessions are offered to seniors, Health Care Card, Pension Card and Companion Card holders, children 15 and under and full-time students. Refunds are issued as gift cards by default; no refund within 72 hours of the event, and earlier cancellations carry a cancellation fee (see the FAQ for the rate).
